name: Lake District Running Festival
course: The 53K passes Scafell Pike and Wasdale; the 23K uses High Spy and Catbells.
transport: Keswick School is the event hub and finish; confirm parking and early arrival
facilities: Bag drop, toilets and staffed aid stations
cutoff: 53K finish by 21:30; check 23K and intermediate limits
rules: Read the route-specific mandatory kit and checkpoint schedule; mountain navigation may be needed.
reason: The two courses are materially different mountain days, not just longer and shorter versions of one loop. The 53K crosses Scafell Pike and has checkpoint deadlines.

name: Cheltenham Running Festival
elevation: 122m on half-marathon route; shorter routes unconfirmed
course: Racecourse setting; check the mapped route for your distance.
transport: Cheltenham Racecourse, GL50 4SH; confirm venue entrance
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: Do not apply the half-marathon ascent figure to the 5K or 10K.
reason: A racecourse venue with three adult distances. The half has a published 122m ascent, while shorter-course climbing needs separate checking.

name: Dartford Half Marathon and 10K
course: Mainly closed-road single loop with an athletics-track finish.
transport: Central Park Arena start and finish; check road closures around Dartford
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: The 12:15 race end is important for slower half-marathon entrants; confirm the exact cut-off.
reason: A single-loop road race finishing on an athletics track. The half starts after the 10K but the event ends at 12:15, so slower runners should confirm the limit.

name: Crystal Palace Running Festival January
course: Undulating park laps: half four plus a mini loop, 10K two, 5K one.
transport: Crystal Palace Park, SE19 2BB; confirm the event entrance
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: Lap counting and the shared 5K/10K start matter; follow the signs for your own distance.
reason: An undulating park circuit rather than a flat city 10K. The half uses more than four laps, making pacing and lap counting central.

name: Crewe 10K
course: Closed-road town-centre route, returning to the event village.
transport: Crewe station about 20 minutes on foot; no dedicated event parking
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: Minimum age 15; check closure and parking plan before driving.
reason: A measured town-centre 10K with modest published climbing and a firm 90-minute road-closure limit. The station is walkable but needs arrival time.

name: The Fox Trail
course: Point-to-point Surrey trail routes with GPX supplied for self-navigation.
transport: Point-to-point event; verify each distance's start and finish shuttle plan
facilities: Bag drop, marked routes, marshals and aid support
rules: Check the route-specific cut-off and GPX before selecting a distance.
reason: Three point-to-point trail distances share a 19:00 event finish. The start location and transport plan need checking for the exact route entered.

name: South Downs Trail August
course: Woodland, grassy tracks and chalk downland from Queen Elizabeth Country Park.
transport: Country-park start and finish; check event parking and access
facilities: Bag drop, aid stations, waymarking and marshals
rules: Compare route-specific climbing, mandatory kit and cut-offs before entering.
reason: A choice from 12K to 50K on mixed South Downs trails. The early 50K start and summer exposure make route and kit checks more useful than the headline distance alone.

name: Running GP Bedford Autodrome August
distance: Marathon / 20 miles / metric marathon / half marathon / 10km / 5km
course: Smooth traffic-free motor circuit with repeated laps.
transport: Bedford Autodrome, MK44 2YP; check circuit access and parking
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: A metric marathon is 26.2km, not 26.2 miles; verify lap count and cut-off.
reason: The traffic-free circuit is useful for controlled pacing across six distances. Entrants must distinguish the 26.2km metric marathon from the full marathon.

name: Running GP Oulton Park August
distance: Marathon / 20 miles / metric marathon / half marathon / 10km / 5km
start: Marathon 09:30 through 5K 11:45; choose the correct distance start.
course: Gently undulating, traffic-free tarmac motor circuit.
transport: Oulton Park Race Circuit; free parking listed by organiser
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: Metric marathon is 26.2km; confirm lap count and time limit for your entry.
reason: A traffic-free circuit but not a level course. Six staggered distance starts and the metric-marathon option require careful entry selection.

name: Draycote Water Running Festival May
course: Reservoir setting; confirm the route and surface for your distance.
transport: Draycote Water country park; check venue parking and access
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: Check the final distance-specific route and cut-off following the venue's reopening.
reason: A returning reservoir event after venue building works. Before comparing it with road 10Ks, check the final surface and route for the chosen distance.
